title: Battle of Adrianople
summary: On 9 August 378 CE, a confederation of Gothic rebels under Fritigern routed the Eastern Roman field army outside Adrianople. Emperor Valens and approximately two-thirds of his forces were killed, inflicting an unprecedented military catastrophe that permanently weakened Roman frontiers.

uncertainty.note: 9 August 378 in the Julian calendar (10 August 378 proleptic Gregorian).

as_recorded.value: fifth before the Ides of August

importance.justification: The destruction of the Eastern Roman field army and death of Emperor Valens crippled Roman military manpower and forced the empire to accommodate autonomous barbarian nations within its borders.

related.because: The battle was the climax of the Gothic War following the crossing of the Danube in 376.

beats.caption: On 9 August 378, Gothic cavalry charges Roman lines outside Adrianople, crushing Valens' army.
Emperor Valens and two-thirds of the eastern field army perish, shattering Roman military dominance in Thrace.

sources.title: Ammianus Marcellinus, Roman History (Res Gestae), Book XXXI
